core.title: Declare coverage exceptions only through allow-lists or in-progress status
core.given: A plan artifact (product capability, feature or DESIRED OUTCOME) intentionally does not satisfy full coverage
core.when: the planner records that coverage gap
core.then: Declare the exception only through the matching coverage-exception allow-list entry or by marking the artifact with the stack's in-progress status — never leave the gap undeclared.
prefer: List product capabilities that are utility, shared or under development in the allow-list for product capabilities not placed in any user/system flow.
List deprecated or experimental features in the allow-list for features no capability/DESIRED_OUTCOME references (orphaned features).
List draft/placeholder DESIRED OUTCOMES in the allow-list for DESIRED OUTCOMES without acceptance.

Mark genuinely unfinished artifacts with the stack's in-progress status; that status exempts them from full coverage only for the coverage findings named by this rule's realization-defined status-exemption scope.
avoid: Leaving a coverage gap with no allow-list entry and no in-progress status.
Allow-listing an artifact in a list whose use case does not fit it (e.g. putting a finished, live product capability in the list for product capabilities not in any user/system flow).
Marking finished artifacts in-progress just to silence coverage checks, or assuming the status exempts from coverage findings outside its realization-defined exemption scope.
core.why: Coverage checks are strict; explicit, recorded exceptions keep intentional gaps visible and reviewable instead of hiding real missing coverage.
evidence: Every coverage gap reported by the detector maps to an entry under the matching coverage-exception allow-list key or to an artifact carrying the in-progress status.
Status exemptions are applied only to the coverage findings named by this rule's realization-defined status-exemption scope.
Each allow-list entry fits its list's use case (utility/shared/under-development product capabilities; deprecated/experimental features; draft/placeholder DESIRED OUTCOMES).
verification: Strict disposition: every coverage gap a check reports must be closed or matched by a declared exception — an allow-list entry in the list whose documented use case fits, or the artifact's in-progress status; an undeclared gap remains a violation.
An allow-list entry excepts a gap only when it sits in the list whose documented use case matches the artifact's situation; the check verifies each entry's use-case fit.
The in-progress status exempts only the coverage findings named by this rule's realization-defined status-exemption scope; every other coverage check still applies to the artifact.

The concrete allow-list keys and the status literal are stack data supplied through the profile; which findings the status exempts is rule-specific disposition defined by this rule's realization, not profile data, and the finding ids of this rule are realization details named generically here.

values: product capability not in user/system flow
product capability not in any user/system flow
artifact status set to or from the in-progress value

fires: Planner adds a utility/shared/under-development product capability that is intentionally not placed in any user/system flow.
Planner keeps a deprecated or experimental feature that no capability/DESIRED_OUTCOME references.
Planner authors a draft or placeholder DESIRED OUTCOME that has no acceptance yet.
A coverage check reports a gap and the planner intends to exempt rather than close it.
doesNotFire: Planner adds a product capability to a user/system flow, or a DESIRED OUTCOME with full acceptance coverage — no exception is needed.
Code-only changes that touch no plan artifact or coverage config.

neutralityNotes: Product capability, user/system flow, feature, DESIRED OUTCOME and acceptance are treated as stack-neutral ATDD plan vocabulary (they are parameters of the closed vocabulary's layout and urn groups), so the core keeps them; only the concrete config keys (coverage.exceptions.*), the path globs / file-name patterns, the status literal (status: draft), and the finding ids (COVERAGE-PLAN-2.1/2.4) and term ids are realization-specific. The allow-list mechanism and the in-progress status representation have no vocabulary entry, so two idiom keys are proposed and also listed in profileRequirements. Per the vocabulary's notProfileKeys boundary, idiom.plan_syntax#coverage_status_exemption carries only the status representation (status: draft); the exemption-scope list — which coverage findings the status exempts — is rule-specific disposition defined by this rule's realization, stated generically in core verification and kept exactly (with its finding ids) in bunOnly, never in the profile. The Bun activation fact names 'layer' and 'path_glob' were mapped to the neutral fact vocabulary as 'role' (plan_artifact) and 'file_kind' (plan_artifact, config). fires/doesNotFire were carried verbatim because they are already plan-level and stack-neutral. Instantiating the core with the Bun profile values plus the bunOnly items reproduces bun.json's obligation exactly: no exception path, use-case condition, or scope limit was dropped, and no new obligation was added.
